title: Welcoming & Seating Guests
blurb: How to greet guests warmly, seat them thoughtfully and read what each guest wants from their visit.
siteNotes: How bookings are checked (system or book) and where accessible tables and highchairs are
Which specials are mentioned at the table each service
legalNotes: No legal rules in this trainer; it is service good practice.

cards.title: Welcoming & Seating Guests
cards.body:
By the end of this session you can:
- greet every guest promptly and warmly
- seat guests with their needs in mind
- read whether a guest wants a chat or quiet

cards.title: The welcome sets the tone
cards.body:
People decide how they feel about a place within moments of walking in. A guest who feels welcomed relaxes and enjoys themselves. One left standing awkwardly at the door does not.

> Get the welcome right and the rest of the visit tends to follow.

items.title: Moments
items.text: Guests form an impression almost at once.

cards.title: Be noticed, be warm
cards.body:
Greet arriving guests promptly, with eye contact and a smile, and make them feel expected. If you are mid-task and cannot seat them that second, still acknowledge them.

> "Welcome! I'll be right with you" works wonders.

cards.title: Think before you seat
cards.body: Check the booking, then think about each guest's needs. Guide them to the table, help with coats or bags if appropriate, present the menus and mention any specials.

items.title: Highchair
items.text: A family with a little one.

items.title: Menus and specials
items.text: Once they are at the table.

cards.title: Not everyone wants the same
cards.body: Some guests want a chat; others just want to settle in quietly. Being welcoming is not about being over-the-top. It is about making everyone feel expected, valued and looked after from the first moment.

right.title: Over-the-top
items: Chatting to a guest who wants quiet

cards.title: Remember
cards.body:
- Greet promptly, with eye contact and a smile
- Acknowledge guests even when you are busy
- Check the booking and think about each guest's needs
- Read the guest: chat or quiet
- The welcome sets the tone for the whole visit

cards.q: Guests form an impression of a place within moments of arriving.
cards.why: People decide how they feel about a place within moments of walking in.

cards.q: You are busy and cannot seat a guest immediately. What should you do?
options: Point to the bar and ask them to find a seat
Carry on with your task until you are free to seat them
Acknowledge them, for example "Welcome, I'll be right with you"
Ask them to wait outside until a table is ready
cards.why: Even mid-task, acknowledge the guest. Nobody likes to feel invisible, and being noticed is the first thing a good welcome does.

cards.q: You should greet arriving guests with…
options: Eye contact and a smile
A clipboard and a list of questions
A friendly wave from across the room
A quick nod while you finish what you are doing
cards.why: A prompt greeting with eye contact and a smile makes guests feel expected.

cards.q: When seating guests you should consider their needs, for example accessibility.
cards.why: An accessible table, a highchair or a quieter corner can all be part of seating well.

cards.q: A good welcome makes guests feel…
options: Hurried towards their table
Lucky to have got a table
Noticed only when they ask
Expected and valued
cards.why: Making everyone feel expected, valued and looked after is the aim of a welcome.

cards.q: Being welcoming means being loud and over-the-top with everyone.
cards.why: Being welcoming is not about being over-the-top. Read the guest.

cards.q: Which of these is a good thing to do after guiding guests to their table?
options: Wait at the table until they are ready to order
Present the menus and mention any specials
Ask them to settle the bill in advance
Leave them to find the menus on their own
cards.why: After guiding guests to the table, help with coats or bags if appropriate, present the menus and mention any specials.

cards.q: Some guests want a chat; others prefer to settle in quietly.
cards.why: Read the guest and match their mood.

cards.q: Before seating, it helps to check the…
options: Menu prices
Weather forecast
Booking
Local news
cards.why: Checking the booking lets you think about each guest's needs before you seat them.

cards.q: The welcome sets the tone for the whole visit.
cards.why: Get the welcome right and the rest of the visit tends to follow.
